The corrupted element is M4. Its width is 142.4 µm, while its reference device M3 is 21.41 µm. That gives a PMOS mirror ratio of about 6.65:1 instead of 1:1, so the output carries about 128 µA (measured 127.6 µA) instead of 20 µA, which matches the 538% error. The sensitivities agree: M4 has the largest effect on iout error (+23.9%), and increasing it lowers rout (-17%), as expected for a larger output current. M3 and M2 are the next most likely contributors to the mirror-ratio error.
